results.name: Record Manual Bill Payments
results.title: Record Manual Bill Payments
results.body:
You can record payments received outside Clio Payments, like cash, checks, wire transfers, or ACH payments, and edit or delete these payments, then track their history. Accurately recording manual bill payments helps keep a client's balance current and your firm's books reconciled. Complete records show what is paid, what is outstanding, and where every payment landed.

Note: If your client paid by credit card or eCheck through Clio Payments, see Record and Manage Online Bill Payments. To record a payment from client trust funds, see Apply Trust Funds to Bills. 

Understand manual payment sources

Direct payment:

Record a payment received outside Clio Payments, such as cash, check, wire transfer, or ACH.

Other:

Record payment from an external platform such as Cash App or Venmo or a credit card processed outside Clio Payments.

Trust account:

Apply trust funds already received at the client or matter level toward a bill.

 

Record a single bill or multi-matter bill payment

You record payment for a single bill and a multi-matter bill the same way. A multi-matter bill is one bill that includes activities for multiple matters belonging to one client.

Note: On a multi-matter bill, payment applies to the oldest created matter first.

  1. Go to the Billing tab, or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select the Unpaid subtab.
  3. In the Actions column, next to Send, click the down arrow and select Record payment.
  4. Select one of the options for the Payment source, the deposit account, payer, and amount paid.
    • When the amount paid is less than the amount due, you can write off the remaining amount and add a description or note.
  5. If you use multiple currencies, and the client's payment currency differs from the bill or deposit account currency, the applicable conversion rate and any conversion loss or gain will be shown at the time of payment:
    • If the payment currency differs from the selected deposit account currency: Losses will be written off if the client paid the invoice amount(s) in full.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an underpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: You can opt to write off the remaining amount.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an overpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: The invoice will be considered paid in full.
  6. Click Record payment.

 

Record payment for one client's multiple bills

Note: You cannot record payments for bills belonging to different clients at the same time.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Billing.
  2. Click Record payment.
  3. Search for the client. All unpaid bills for that client appear.
  4. Select one of the options for the Payment source, the deposit account, payer, and amount paid. 
    • When the amount paid is less than the amount due, you can write off the remaining amount and add a description or note.
  5. If you use multiple currencies, and the client's payment currency differs from the bill or deposit account currency, the applicable conversion rate and any conversion loss or gain will be shown at the time of payment:
    • If the payment currency differs from the selected deposit account currency: Losses will be written off if the client paid the invoice amount(s) in full.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an underpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: You can opt to write off the remaining amount.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an overpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: The invoice will be considered paid in full.
  6. Click Record payment.

 

Record bill payments from trust funds

If your client has trust funds on the client or matter level, you can record payment for a bill from the trust funds. You can record payment and apply trust funds at the same time as the bill approval process or after a bill has already been approved. The bill moves to paid, or shows the remaining balance when trust funds do not cover the full amount.

When paying bills with client-level trust funds, Clio Manage generates three distinct transactions to accurately represent the movement of funds. These transactions record: a transfer to the matter balance (the system prevents edits to this transaction), a transfer from the client-level trust funds, and a transfer to your operating account to pay the invoice.

Note: If the trust funds are not sufficient to cover the total bill payment, the bill will remain in the Unpaid state with the remaining balance.

Note: If evergreen trust is enabled for the matter, applying trust funds to a bill can automatically generate a new replenishment trust request and clear the matter's existing trust request using the Clear old trust requests to prevent duplicates checkbox. Learn more about evergreen trust replenishment.

Apply trust to individual bills

Approve bill and apply trust funds Apply trust funds to approved bill
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select either the Draft or Pending approval subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select Approve & apply trust.
  4. Select your operating account as the destination account for payment.
  5. Click Approve & apply trust.
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select the Unpaid subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Send and select Record payment. You can also click Record payment in the upper right corner.
  4. If your client has trust funds, you will see a table showing the amounts on the matter and contact levels. From the Source dropdown, select your client’s trust funds.
  5. Complete the remaining details.
  6. Click Record payment.
Tip: For a quicker way to apply trust funds to a bill, in step 3, click the down arrow next to Send and select Apply trust funds. Then, select the destination account and click Apply trust.

 

Apply trust to multiple bills

You can also perform bulk actions to approve bills or to apply trust to approved bills

Approve bills and apply trust funds Apply trust funds to approved bills
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select either the Draft or Pending approval subtab.
  3. Use the checkboxes to select relevant bills.
    • Make sure not to select any trust requests. If you accidentally do select a trust request, it will be excluded from the next action.
  4. Click the down arrow at the top of the table and select Approve & apply trust.
  5. Select your operating account as the destination account for payment.
  6. Click Approve & apply trust.
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select the Unpaid subtab.
  3. Use the checkboxes to select relevant bills.
    • Make sure not to select any trust requests. If you accidentally do select a trust request, it will be excluded from the next action.
  4. Click the down arrow at the top of the table and select Apply trust.
    • A modal will appear with a summary list of the funds that will be applied to each bill. The summary list will only provide details of funds available to apply to the bills you selected. If you selected a bill, but no funds are available, no further action will occur for that bill.
  5. Select the destination account.
  6. Click Apply trust.

The Job status page will show you which bills were successfully approved and trust applied (Apply trust complete) and which bills were approved without applying trust (Approve invoice complete). The latter scenario occurs if no trust funds are available.

 

View bill payment history

After a payment is recorded, you can see which firm user recorded it in three places:

Bill Timeline:

Open a bill and, under Bill Timeline, view its creation and payment history.

Firm Feed:

Go to Dashboard > Firm Feed, click Filter, and under Type select Bill payment or Trust request payment.

Matter Timeline:

Open the matter Dashboard, scroll to Timeline, and filter by bill payment or trust request.

 

Up next

  • Edit and Delete Bill Payments: Change or remove a recorded bill payment.
  • Record Payments on Trust Requests: Record a client's trust deposit before you apply it to a bill.

results.title: Task Lists
results.body:
Task lists are templates or groups of multiple related tasks in Clio Manage that you can assign to yourself or other firm users. With tasks lists, you can assign groupings of tasks in a single step.

Note: Tasks lists are visible to all firm users, and any user can create or edit a task list.

Create task lists

  1. Go to Tasks > Task lists.
  2. Select New task list.
  3. Enter the name of the task list. The description and practice area are optional fields.
  4. Click Save and add tasks to add individual tasks to the task list.
  5. Click Add task template.

    • Enter basic information for the first task in this task list.

      Tip: When adding the description, you can use text formatting like bold, italics, or underline to emphasize critical details or use lists to organize content. You can also add links to the description to reference other information, both in and outside of Clio Manage. For information in Clio Manage, you can copy the link address to any link in Clio Manage (use right click (Windows) or control + click (Mac OS), then Copy Link Address), then return to your description to paste the link.
    • Choose whom to assign the task to.
      • Use list assignee: Use this option if you want the person to whom you assign the task list to also be assigned this task.

      • Select assignee: Use this option if you want a specific person to perform this task, regardless of who is assigned the task list.

        Note: This option can still be overruled at the time that the task list is assigned.
    • Choose a due date for the task.
  6. Click Save and create another to add another task to the task list.
  7. Click Save task template when you are finished adding all tasks to this task list.

Tip: Since tasks in a task list cannot be re-ordered, you can delete the tasks in the list and create new tasks to change the order. You can also rename the tasks by adding numbers in front of the name. This will automatically sort the tasks in ascending numerical order.

 

Edit task lists

When editing a task list, you can do a simple edit by editing the name and description of the list itself or change all information associated with the tasks within that task list.

Simple edit Edit all information
  1. Go to Tasks > Task list.
  2. Click the arrow next to View and select Edit list details.
  3. You can now rename the task list, change the description, and update the practice area.
  4. Click Save details.
  1. Go to Tasks > Task list.
  2. Click the name of the task list or click View.
  3. Click Edit next to the task you want to update.
  4. After updating that task, click Save task template.

 

Assign task lists

You can assign previously created tasks lists to any Clio Manage user at your firm. Follow the steps below to assign a task list from the main Tasks page.

Note: You can only assign users to task lists. If you need to assign a contact to a task, you need to create a single task.

Assign task list via Tasks page Assign task list in matter
  1. Go to Tasks > Task lists.
  2. Click View to see the tasks in the task list or click the down arrow next to View and select Assign list.
  3. Select the assignee, the matter, and the trigger date. Learn more about trigger and due dates in the section below.
  4. Optional: If you want all tasks in the task list to be assigned to your selected assignee, regardless of any specific assignees that you may have previously selected when you created a task in the task list, check the box for Assign all tasks in this list to this assignee.
  5. Optional: You can notify the task assignee(s) via email by checking the relevant box.
  6. Click Assign task list. You can now find the tasks in this list in the Tasks subtab of the matter.
  1. Go to the matter and click the Tasks subtab.
  2. Select Assign task list.
  3. Choose the task list, the assignee, and the trigger date. Learn more about trigger and due dates in the section below.
  4. Optional: If you want all tasks in the task list to be assigned to your selected assignee, regardless of any specific assignees that you may have previously selected when you created a task in the task list, check the box for Assign all tasks in this list to this assignee.
  5. Optional: You can notify the task assignee(s) via email by checking the relevant box.
  6. Click Assign task list.

Tip: You can also assign an individual task within a task list rather than the entire task list. With the task list open, click the down arrow next to Edit and select Assign task template.

 

Set trigger and relative due date

When creating or editing a task list, you can set whether the tasks in the list should all be due on a specific date or whether the due dates should vary depending on other tasks in the task list.

If you use a trigger date for the tasks in a task list, all the tasks in the list will be due on the selected trigger date. You can set the trigger date when assigning the task list.

If you select a relative due date, you can specify the due date of one task in relation to the trigger date of another task. This means that you can select a specific due date for your first task in the task list and set the second task to be due a set number of time before or after the first task in the task list.

Note: You cannot change the due date of tasks in a task list if the task list has already been assigned.

 

Duplicate task lists

If you need to quickly create multiple similar tasks lists, you can use the duplicate function on an existing task list. When you duplicate a task list, it will also duplicate the tasks within the task list.

  1. Go to Tasks > Task lists.
  2. Click the down arrow next to View and select Duplicate list.
  3. Change the name, description, and practice area for the new task list.
  4. Click Save and edit tasks to update the tasks within the new list.
  5. Click Edit next to the tasks in the list to update them and then save your changes.

 

Delete task lists

When deleting a task list, you can either delete the entire task list and all its subsequent tasks or remove individual tasks within a task list. Existing tasks will not be removed if you delete a task list or tasks within a task list.

Delete task list Remove tasks in task list
  1. Go to Tasks > Task lists.
  2. Click the down arrow next to View and select Delete list.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete.
  1. Go to Tasks > Task lists.
  2. Click the task list name or click View.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select, Delete task template.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete.
Note: If you use automated workflows, make sure that the task list you want to delete is not used by one of your workflows.

There are two methods for exporting data from Trial Works: by requesting a backup from their database and accessing the backup using Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio Express (option 1), or by exporting using their reports functionality to export contacts, clients, and matters (option 2).

Option 1

Step 1: Contact TrialWorks to request a backup of the TrialWorks database.

Step 2: Follow these steps to access the data in your backup:

  1. Open SQL Server Management Studio Express and connect to the SQL server.
  2. Expand Databases.
  3. Right-click on the database you want to back up, and then select Tasks > Back up (this is not available for version 2018/2019).
  4. On the Back Up Database window, make sure the Database field contains the name of the database you want to back up.
  5. Select Full for the Backup Type.
  6. Click Remove to remove the default/last backup file name.
  7. Click Add to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  8. Click [...] next to the File Name field.
  9. On the Locate Database Files window, select the folder where you want the backup file to go. By default, it is ..\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.1\MSSQL\Backup.
  10. In the File Name field, type the name for this backup, with a .bak extension. For example,xyz_20080221.bak for a backup of the XYZ database created on 21 February 2008.
  11. Click OK to close the Locate Database Files window.
  12. Click OK to close the Select Backup Destination window.
  13. Click OK to start the backup. The progress icon displays in the lower-left corner, and a completed successfully message displays when it is done.
